correctness.rationale: A birth adds d_U+ξ edges. For two-stars, old neighbors contribute Σ_(w~U)d_w, linking the parent contributes ξd_U, and the new vertex contributes choose(d_U+ξ,2). Using Σd=2E and Σd²=2S+2E recovers all three conditional recurrences and their stated polynomial solutions with the singleton initial values. (E_n−EE_n)/(n(n+1)) is bounded and has constant conditional expectation because centered increments multiply the previous centered count by (n+2)/n. This gives almost-sure and L² convergence of F_n and its limiting moments; the complement couples the same parent sequence with flipped coins, including deterministic endpoints. An independent check encodes the graph by a binary split tree with one coin per internal vertex: conditional on the tree, Var(E_n)=r(1−r) times Σ_v (a_v b_v)^2, with child leaf counts a_v,b_v. For an ordered root split the first subtree size is uniform on 1,…,n−1 by the unit-seeded Pólya urn, and the within-subtree choices are uniform conditional on the sizes. Thus H_1=0 and (n−1)H_n=Σ_{a=1}^{n−1}[(a(n−a))²+H_a+H_(n−a)] for the expectation of the sum. Substitution or the power-sum identity Σ a²(n−a)²=(n⁵−n)/30 gives H_n=n(n−1)(n²+n+3)/18. A bounded replay of this recurrence in scaled integers J_n=18H_n checked orders 2–64 (J_2 through J_5 are 18,90,276,660). The limit proof is not based on that bounded check.
